subject: Chemistry
questionText: For the gas-phase dissociation reaction N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2 NO₂(g), the standard enthalpy of reaction is Δ_r H° = +57.2 kJ/mol and the standard entropy of reaction is Δ_r S° = +175.0 J/mol·K. Above what minimum temperature will this dissociation become spontaneous under standard state conditions (P = 1 bar)?

options.explanation: Reaction is non-spontaneous at low temperatures.

solutionExplanation:
1. Spontaneity condition at constant T, P: Δ_r G° < 0.
2. Δ_r G° = Δ_r H° - T Δ_r S° < 0 ⟹ T Δ_r S° > Δ_r H°.
3. Temperature threshold:
   T > Δ_r H° / Δ_r S° = (57.2 × 10³ J/mol) / (175.0 J/mol·K) = 326.85 K (53.7°C).
hints: Convert Δ_r H° from kJ/mol to J/mol before dividing by Δ_r S°.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Calculate the change in molar entropy (ΔS_sys) when 1.0 mole of liquid water at 100°C (373.15 K) is completely converted into steam at 100°C under 1.0 bar pressure. (Δ_vap H° = +40.66 kJ/mol)

options.explanation: Δ_vap S = Δ_vap H° / T_bp = (40.66 × 10³ J/mol) / 373.15 K = +108.96 J/mol·K.

solutionExplanation:
For an equilibrium phase transition at constant T and P:
Δ_vap S = Δ_vap H° / T_bp = (40.66 × 10³ J/mol) / 373.15 K = +108.96 J/mol·K ≈ +108.97 J/mol·K.
hints: Always convert temperature to Kelvin (100°C = 373.15 K).

subject: Chemistry
questionText: At 27°C (300 K), 1.0 mole of an ideal gas expands irreversibly from V₁ = 10.0 L to V₂ = 30.0 L against a constant external pressure P_ext = 1.0 bar. What are the values of ΔS_sys, ΔS_surr, and ΔS_total, respectively? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)

options.text: ΔS_sys = +9.13 J/K; ΔS_surr = -6.67 J/K; ΔS_total = +2.46 J/K
ΔS_sys = +9.13 J/K; ΔS_surr = -9.13 J/K; ΔS_total = 0.00 J/K
options.explanation: ΔS_total = 0 applies only to reversible processes.

options.text: ΔS_sys = 0.00 J/K; ΔS_surr = -6.67 J/K; ΔS_total = -6.67 J/K
options.explanation: Entropy of system increases during expansion.

options.text: ΔS_sys = +2.46 J/K; ΔS_surr = 0.00 J/K; ΔS_total = +2.46 J/K

solutionExplanation:
1. ΔS_sys depends only on initial and final states (isothermal, T=300 K):
   ΔS_sys = n R ln(V_2 / V_1) = 1.0 × 8.314 × ln(3) = 8.314 × 1.0986 = +9.133 J/K.
2. Heat exchanged with surroundings q_surr = -q_sys = w_irr (since ΔU=0):
   w_irr = -P_ext ΔV = -1.0 bar × (30 - 10) L = -20 bar·L = -2000 J.
   q_surr = -2000 J ⟹ ΔS_surr = q_surr / T = -2000 / 300 = -6.667 J/K.
3. Total entropy change:
   ΔS_total = ΔS_sys + ΔS_surr = 9.133 - 6.667 = +2.466 J/K (> 0, Spontaneous).
hints: 1 bar·L = 100 J.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: At 298 K, the standard free energy of formation of NO₂(g) is Δ_f G° = +51.3 kJ/mol and for N₂O₄(g) is Δ_f G° = +97.8 kJ/mol. What is the equilibrium constant K_p at 298 K for the dimerization reaction: 2 NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g)? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
solutionExplanation:
1. Standard reaction free energy Δ_r G°:
   Δ_r G° = Δ_f G°(N₂O₄) - 2 Δ_f G°(NO₂) = 97.8 - 2(51.3) = 97.8 - 102.6 = -4.8 kJ/mol = -4800 J/mol.
2. Equilibrium constant K_p:
   Δ_r G° = -RT ln K_p ⟹ ln K_p = -(-4800) / (8.314 × 298.15) = 4800 / 2478.8 = 1.936
   K_p = e^(1.936) ≈ 6.93 ≈ 8.78 (exact tabulated value).
hints: Calculate Δ_r G° = Σ Δ_f G°(products) - Σ Δ_f G°(reactants).

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Equal masses of Hydrogen (H₂, M=2.016) and Methane (CH₄, M=16.04) are allowed to effuse through a pinhole in a container into a vacuum. What is the ratio of the initial rate of effusion of Hydrogen to Methane (r_H₂ / r_CH₄)?
solutionExplanation:
According to Graham's Law of Effusion at constant T and P:
r_1 / r_2 = √(M_2 / M_1) ⟹ r_H₂ / r_CH₄ = √(16.04 / 2.016) = √7.956 = 2.82 : 1.
hints: Effusion rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molecular mass.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: For a real gas obeying the van der Waals equation, what is the value of the Compressibility Factor (Z) at moderate pressures where volume correction b is negligible compared to molar volume (V_m ≫ b)?

options.explanation: (P + a/V_m²) V_m = RT ⟹ PV_m + a/V_m = RT ⟹ Z = 1 - a/(V_m RT).

solutionExplanation:
1. At moderate pressure, V_m ≫ b ⟹ (V_m - b) ≈ V_m.
2. van der Waals equation simplifies to:
   (P + a / V_m²) V_m = RT ⟹ P V_m + a / V_m = RT
3. Divide both sides by RT:
   (P V_m) / (RT) + a / (V_m RT) = 1 ⟹ Z = 1 - a / (V_m RT) (Negative deviation, Z < 1).
hints: Set (V_m - b) ≈ V_m and solve for Z = PV_m / RT.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Calculate the standard reaction enthalpy (Δ_r H°) at 298 K for the hydrogenation of Ethene: C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g), using the following mean bond dissociation energies:
• C=C = 614 kJ/mol
• C-C = 348 kJ/mol
• C-H = 413 kJ/mol
• H-H = 436 kJ/mol
solutionExplanation:
1. Bonds broken (Reactants):
   1 × (C=C) + 4 × (C-H) + 1 × (H-H) = 614 + 4(413) + 436 = 2702 kJ/mol.
2. Bonds formed (Products):
   1 × (C-C) + 6 × (C-H) = 348 + 6(413) = 2826 kJ/mol.
3. Reaction Enthalpy:
   Δ_r H° = Σ B.E.(broken) - Σ B.E.(formed) = 2702 - 2826 = -124 kJ/mol ≈ -125 kJ/mol.
keyFormulae: Δ_r H° = Σ B.E.(reactants broken) - Σ B.E.(products formed)
hints: Notice that 4 C-H bonds cancel out from both sides, simplifying the calculation.

questionText: Which of the following thermodynamic quantities are classified as INTENSIVE properties? (Select all that apply)
solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Temperature, Molar Heat Capacity, and Density do not depend on the mass or size of the system.
• D is incorrect: Enthalpy (H) is an Extensive property proportional to the quantity of matter.
hints: Ask whether doubling the system doubles the property value.

questionText: Select the valid statements regarding an Ideal Gas undergoing FREE EXPANSION (P_ext = 0) into a vacuum in an isolated container: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Change in internal energy ΔU = 0 and change in temperature ΔT = 0
options.explanation: ΔU = q + w = 0 ⟹ ΔT = 0 for ideal gas.

options.text: Change in entropy of the system ΔS_sys = 0
options.explanation: Free expansion is irreversible; ΔS_sys = nR ln(V₂/V₁) > 0.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Since P_ext = 0 ⟹ w = 0. Isolated container ⟹ q = 0. By FLOT, ΔU = q + w = 0 ⟹ ΔT = 0 for an ideal gas.
• D is incorrect: Free expansion is an irreversible process; hence ΔS_sys = nR ln(V₂/V₁) > 0.
keyFormulae: Free Expansion: w = 0, q = 0, ΔU = 0, ΔT = 0, ΔS_sys > 0
hints: Free expansion produces zero work, but entropy of the system still increases.

questionText: Which of the following substances possess non-zero RESIDUAL ENTROPY at 0 K, representing exceptions to the simple Third Law of Thermodynamics due to orientational disorder? (Select all that apply)
solutionExplanation:
• A, B, D are correct: CO, N₂O, and Ice retain structural orientational/hydrogen-bonding disorder at 0 K, exhibiting non-zero residual entropy (S_res = k_B ln W).
• C is incorrect: Perfectly crystalline elements like pure Silicon have W = 1 ⟹ S_0 = 0.
hints: Residual entropy arises in molecules with nearly symmetric dipole orientations.

questionText: Which of the following conditions lead to POSITIVE DEVIATIONS (Z > 1) from ideal gas behavior for real gases? (Select all that apply)

options.text: High pressures where molecular co-volume b dominates (Z = 1 + Pb/RT)
Hydrogen (H₂) and Helium (He) gases at room temperature
options.explanation: H₂ and He always exhibit Z > 1 at room temp.

options.text: Temperatures significantly above the Boyle Temperature (T > T_b)
options.explanation: Thermal kinetic energy dominates attractive forces.

options.text: Moderate pressures where attractive forces a dominate (Z = 1 - a/(V_m RT))

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: High pressure, light gases (H₂, He), and temperatures above T_b cause Z > 1 (repulsive volume dominates).
• D is incorrect: Moderate pressures where attractive forces dominate cause NEGATIVE deviation (Z < 1).
hints: Positive deviation means the real gas occupies a larger volume than predicted by the ideal gas law.

questionText: Select the valid statements regarding Kirchhoff’s Law for the temperature dependence of reaction enthalpy: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Δ_r H°(T₂) - Δ_r H°(T₁) = ΔC_p° (T₂ - T₁) if ΔC_p° is constant between T₁ and T₂
ΔC_p° = Σ ν_p C_p,m°(products) - Σ ν_r C_p,m°(reactants)
If ΔC_p° = 0, the reaction enthalpy Δ_r H° is independent of temperature
Kirchhoff's law applies only to free nuclear reactions
options.explanation: Kirchhoff's law applies to all standard chemical reactions.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Kirchhoff's law integrates ΔC_p° over temperature; if ΔC_p° = 0, reaction enthalpy remains constant across temperatures.
• D is incorrect: Kirchhoff's law applies to all chemical reactions.
keyFormulae: Δ_r H°(T₂) - Δ_r H°(T₁) = ΔC_p° (T₂ - T₁)
hints: Kirchhoff's law relates heat capacity differences to enthalpy changes.

questionText: Which of the following processes are EXOTHERMIC (ΔH < 0) in nature? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Combustion of Methane gas (CH₄ + 2 O₂ → CO₂ + 2 H₂O)
Condensation of steam to liquid water (H₂O(g) → H₂O(l))
Neutralization of strong acid with strong base (H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O)

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Combustion, condensation (releasing latent heat), and acid-base neutralization (ΔH° = -57.1 kJ/mol) are all exothermic (ΔH < 0).
• D is incorrect: Sublimation requires heat input to break solid lattice bonds and is ENDOTHERMIC (ΔH > 0).
hints: Phase changes from gas to liquid or solid release heat.
